title: A review range too large for one Critic is split per module, so a whole-feature review never ends at the budget ceiling without a verdict
goal: Candidate 20e, G20-72 (PO tile decision 2026-11-08: split per module; never touch the Critic preimage pin, agents/critic.md maxTurns stays 65). MEASURED in the Claude greenfield TabletApp_claude_070_3 (2026-11-08): the full-feature Critic (whole range 5827554..bf8e9e9, about 10 modules, 287 tests) hit DISPATCH-BUDGET-CHECKPOINT at call 40 of 50 still in Phase 1 without a verdict; the coordinator's grant of +40 was refused (headroom 9: maxTurns 65 - closing 5 - 1 - base 50), so a Critic can never exceed 59 working calls. STEP 1 (measure, no edit): read how one review round binds exactly one packet and one fresh Critic session (critic-dispatch-preflight packet-ready, critic-generic-batch round reservation CGB-BUDGET, session-critic-finalizer admit/finalize, the receipt's session block) and write the finding into the notes: can one round carry N Critic children (one per module) whose verdicts merge into the one round verdict WITHOUT weakening any check (fresh context per child, path-only input, evidence-gated verdict, one receipt per round)? STEP 2 (build, only if step 1 says yes): the packet-ready result gains an additive `split` field when the reviewed range exceeds a size bound derived from the Critic's working cap (name the bound and its derivation in one constant, for example changed files or changed lines per 50 calls, measured from the greenfield range): one entry per module of the approved architecture module plan (the same module cut lib/module-dispatch-scope.mjs uses) with its exact path-only reviewerInput (a reviewScope of that module's owned paths plus the shared spec, guardrails and evidence paths), and the coordinator-facing next step: dispatch one Critic per entry, then merge their verdict files with one named command into the single round verdict that admit/finalize already accept; the merge refuses a missing child, a child outside its scope, or a duplicate finding id. A range below the bound keeps today's result byte for byte. Runner-neutral wording. STEP 3: regression cases: a range above the bound yields one split entry per module with disjoint scopes covering every changed path (a changed path owned by no module goes into a shared entry, never dropped); below the bound no split field; the merge refuses each of its three cases; the finalized receipt of a merged round verifies.
